$comment: THE PUBLICATION POLICY — what is IN THE GAME (maintainer 2026-08-14).
This file is the ONLY hand-maintained part of the split. Everything else is
derived by scripts/shipset.mjs, which closes over these roots: a published
world drags in its own tiles, its NPCs' character art and its spawn zones'
monsters automatically. Add an NPC to a shipped world and its art ships with
Anything NOT reachable from these roots is STAGING content: it stays in git,
stays reviewable in the wiki for a signed-in admin (fetched from GitHub), and
Editing this file changes what production serves. The shipset digest changes
with it, which is what makes the image and the tile atlas rebuild.
$comment_userWorlds: THE GAME. What an end user may select, and — since 2026-08-15 — the ONLY
worlds the image carries: the ship-set closure walks this list, nothing
else. A product gate, not a security boundary (the repo is public); the
point is the game never OFFERS anything else.
A name may live in EITHER world tree — maps2/worlds (world@1/@2) or
maps2/worlds3 (pixel-maps3) — resolved by probing, so this list names a
world and nothing else. the_game is the default map (maintainer 2026-09-02:
the new default, and once we are happy with it the only playable map;
until then the_island2 stays). A worlds3 world ships its own docs, its
NPC/monster closure and its placed scenery pieces from here, and its
TERRAIN ART as the tiles3 resolver's exact closure, computed in the
Dockerfile's build stage by scripts/ship-tiles3.ts (measured on the_game:
508 files / 0.3 MB of the 400 MB tiles/ domain).
$comment_devWorlds3: STAGING worlds in the SECOND world tree, maps2/worlds3/<name>/world.json
(pixel-maps3/world@1 — a ground NAME per cell, no baked tile art; tiles3
resolves what draws at draw time). Same staging contract as devWorlds and
the same zero bytes in the image; a separate key because the name alone
cannot say which directory holds the world, and the client's fetches, the
server's readWorldDoc and shipset's policy check all have to know.
Joining one also streams the tiles3 ART TREES (tiles/plates, tiles/patterns,
tiles/tops, tiles/fades, tiles/base_candidates, tiles/review + the index
JSONs) from the CDN through the same gameUrl chokepoint: they are served at
/assets/tiles/... and the image ships only the closure of its PUBLISHED
worlds3 worlds (userWorlds above), never the 400 MB domain.
$comment_devWorlds: STAGING worlds: renderer test beds and generator fixtures. NOT in the
image at all — an admin who joins one streams it from the repo (client:
staging.ts via jsDelivr; server: WorldRoom's disk-first GitHub fallback).
They cost production zero bytes, which is what lets monster_demo one day
spawn all 57 monsters without dragging 16 MB of monster art into the
container (the leak the maintainer caught 2026-08-15). The admin picker
reads this list via the CDN; the dev server still plays them from the
$comment_monsters: Monsters reachable from a published world's spawns.json are found
automatically. This list is only for monsters the ENGINE names directly
with no spawn zone — leave empty unless something 404s.
$comment_scenery: The three pieces WorldScene loads by hardcoded path. The v2 factory's other
~2,640 pieces are staging content until the maps2 agent places them.
$comment_entityDomains: Domains where individual entities are selected by closure. Their ROOT-level
files and config/ trees ship wholesale regardless — those are descriptors the
characters2/animation_map.json, tiles2/emission.json). Omitting one does not
404 a sprite, it silently empties a manifest: the first curated root built a
game with ZERO monsters for exactly this reason.
$comment_alwaysShip: Domains where per-entity closure buys little: items and lore are small and
wholly in-game, live/ is runtime tuning state, wiki/ is the wiki itself.
sounds/ and music/ are catalog-driven at runtime rather than referenced by
the worlds, so they ship whole minus the excludes below — tightening those
two to a real catalog closure is a follow-up, not a guess to make here.
$comment_exclude: Applied last, so these carve out of the wholesale alwaysShip includes.
tiles2/*/raw and the music masters were already excluded by .dockerignore —
kept here so ONE file is the source of truth for what ships.
